content: Godot 4.7 Android joypad API facts. (1) Android uses Java InputDevice via JNI, not SDL: joyconnectionchanged passes only (device, connected, name) so get_joy_guid() returns a hex encoding of the device name, not an SDL GUID; get_joy_info() is documented as always empty on Android and Web; is_joy_known() is always false. Use get_joy_name() for identification. (2) No SDL controller DB on Android: fallback_mapping is -1 for non-XR apps, so Input::joy_axis() takes the raw path and Godot axis indices equal the ordinal position of the Android AXIS_* constants after Collections.sort() - for typical BT pads X,Y,Z,RZ,LTRIGGER,RTRIGGER sort to 0..5, matching LEFT_X,LEFT_Y,RIGHT_X,RIGHT_Y,TRIGGER_LEFT,TRIGGER_RIGHT. Buttons are safe: getGodotButton maps KEYCODE_BUTTON_A/B/X/Y to 0/1/2/3. (3) Triggers arrive as 0..1 on Android vs -1..1 on desktop (input.cpp has an #ifndef ANDROID_ENABLED branch). (4) Input.get_joy_axis returns raw undeadzoned values; Godot's built-in deadzone (default 0.5) only applies to InputMap actions and Input.get_vector, so gesture code must implement its own deadzone.
